story: How a 1% fee can quietly take 22% of your money

segments.label: MONEY LAB
segments.title: A 1% fee. 22% of your money.
segments.narration: A one percent fee sounds small. Over thirty years it can take about 22 percent of your money.

segments.label: THE SETUP
segments.title: $100,000, 7% a year, 30 years
segments.point: Fund A fee 0.1%. Fund B fee 1%.
segments.narration: Invest one hundred thousand dollars earning seven percent a year for thirty years. Fund A charges point one percent. Fund B charges one percent.

segments.label: 30 YEARS LATER
segments.title: Same market, different fee
segments.narration: Fund A grows to about 740,000 dollars. Fund B grows to about 574,000.

segments.label: THE MATH
segments.title: The gap: $165,820
segments.point: Fees come off the growth, every year
segments.narration: That is a gap of about 166,000 dollars, because the fee is taken from a growing balance every single year.

segments.label: THE LESSON
segments.title: Check the expense ratio
segments.point: Small percentages compound into big dollars
segments.narration: Before choosing a fund, check its yearly fee. Over decades, it matters as much as the returns.

segments.title: The math behind money
